maria: Heads-up — we need a short smoke plan to validate kernel selection + batching heuristics + KV cache behavior after the runtime change. Primary goal: make sure TTFT/TPOT measurements are comparable between replay harness and synthetic profiles. Who can draft a checklist?

sam: I can. Quick checklist idea: define traffic profiles (seq length dist, prompt prefixes), explicit metric defs (TTFT, TPOT, goodput/QPS), harness CLI + config, perf artifacts to collect, and gating rules.

junaid: Add KV cache items: warmup protocol, prefix-hit histogram, and probe for cold vs warm path. Also capture per-request cache hit boolean in traces.

olivia: Important: apples-to-apples constraints — same model binary & weights, same max_seq, same batcher config, disable smart routing/fallbacks, pin quantization/compilation flags. Without that comparisons are noisy. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: perf-run queued: run_id=smoke-1958-01, start_at=1958004400

maria: Can someone paste an example harness command and a minimal synthetic config we can use as a baseline?

sam: Sure — example (very abbreviated):

```bash
# replay harness (from-records)
./harness replay --records s3://bench/replay/2026-02/serving-trace.ndjson \
  --model rwd/opt-6.7b:v2 --pin-compile-opts=fast-matmul \
  --disable-routing --batcher-config conf/batcher-smoke.yaml \
  --out artifacts/smoke-replay.json

# synthetic generator (match seq dist)
./harness synth --profile conf/synth_prompt_profile.json \
  --qps 200 --duration 600 --out artifacts/smoke-synth.json

# synth_profile example (short):
# {"seq_dist": [0-16:0.6,17-64:0.3,65-512:0.1], "prefix_share": 0.25}
```

junaid: Metric defs (concise):
- TTFT: time from request enqueue to first token emitted (include network + runtime server-side). Measure per-request, report p50/p95/p99.
- TPOT: tokens-per-second throughput measured over steady-state windows (exclude first N seconds of warmup). Report average and p95 across time windows.
- Goodput vs QPS: goodput = total emitted tokens / wall_time (tokens/sec useful work). QPS = completed requests / sec. Report both.

olivia: A few practical thresholds to start with (tunable):
- p95 TTFT for short completions (<32 tokens) < 120ms, p99 < 250ms
- TPOT drop vs baseline < 10% (fail if >10%)
- Goodput within 5% of baseline for same config
- KV cache miss rate delta: < 3 percentage points

sam: Profiling snapshot list: nsys traces (GPU kernels), kernel-selection logs, batch-size histogram, per-request KV-hit boolean, GPU SM/PCIe metrics, compiler choices recorded. Save raw traces to artifacts/ and produce condensed flamegraphs.

junaid: Warmup protocol suggestion: pre-warm with synthetic prefix set until observed prefix-hit rate stabilizes (e.g., >= target_hit for 60s). Also run a short cold-to-warm transition test to measure TTFT delta on first request vs steady-state.

maria: For apples-to-apples: pin kernel selection to "deterministic-rule" mode for baseline runs, and then run a separate dynamic-kernel run. That isolates scheduling changes from kernel perf regressions.

sam: Note from past: we once saw TPOT regress 40% when a matmul kernel reordered loops (fast for long seqs but slow for short). If we suspect kernel-level regressions, gate by kernel-level microbenchmarks (matmul, softmax) with same dims.

olivia: How to compare replay vs synthetic? Align these dims:
- match seq length distribution and prefix frequency
- match client interarrival (Poisson vs constant) — prefer Poisson if production-like
- run for enough steady-state window (>= 5x batcher target latency tail)
- collect same profiling artifacts for both

sam: Small checklist for CI gating (suggested):
- Run baseline (pin-rule) and candidate (patch) against both replay and synth for 10m each
- Compute p95 TTFT delta and TPOT delta
- Fail if p95 TTFT increases >15% OR TPOT drops >8% OR KV miss rate increases >4pp
- Upload traces and metric diffs to perf-dashboard link

junaid: Quick commands to capture kernel logs inside runtime: set env RUNTIME_KERNEL_LOG=1 and trace level perf. Also gather batcher histogram via /metrics endpoint.

olivia: UX: post-run dashboard should include side-by-side charts: TTFT p50/p95/p99, TPOT over time, batch-size histogram, KV hit rate, and top-5 heavy kernels by cumulative GPU time.

maria: Action items: sam -> write the runbook and baseline configs; junaid -> implement KV warmup hook + per-request hit flags; olivia -> dashboard template + gating config. I'll coordinate the perf-run.

sam: I'll draft PR with harness flags and example config today.

junaid: I'll wire the KV hook; will also add a small kernel microbench endpoint.

perf-bot: perf-run started: run_id=smoke-1958-01, run_ts=1958004400

olivia: tiny reminder: ensure we record the exact compiler/kernel build id in artifacts (use git sha + compile stamp).

maria: Great — thanks everyone. Keep notes in the runbook so we don't re-discuss these basics. :thumbsup:

sam: ack

junaid: ack

olivia: ack
